name: service_arms
prompt:
One image: a sprite sheet of 18 tow-truck wheel-lift arms for a 2D top-down city game, seen straight down from above.

Image 1 is the layout: 18 light grey boxes on magenta, numbered left to right and top to bottom, five to a row. Draw one arm in each box, filling the box from its left edge to its right edge and from its top to its bottom, and nothing outside it. Everything outside the arms — the magenta and the gaps — comes back fully transparent: no colour, no glow, no shadow.

Image 2 shows three of the tow trucks these arms belong to: match their art style exactly — outline weight, crisp dark outlines, hard-edged shading, the dark diamond-plate steel, the orange-yellow paint, the red and white hazard stripes, the level of detail. Image 3 is the old arm, extended on the left and folded on the right: the same machine, to be redrawn in image 2's style.

The arm is an underlift that tows a broken car behind the truck by lifting its wheels. In every box it lies along the box, its HINGE at the LEFT and its FORK at the RIGHT (the thick right edge of each box):
- THE ODD BOXES (1, 3, 5 … 17, the larger ones) hold the arm EXTENDED: at the left, a heavy dark steel hinge block with a hydraulic ram and two diagonal struts, about a fifth of the box's length; from it a straight square-section telescopic boom runs right along the box's middle, painted orange-yellow with dark steel joints; at the right end, a crossbar at right angles to the boom spanning the box's whole height, painted in red and white diagonal hazard stripes, with an L-shaped dark steel wheel cradle at each end of the crossbar opening towards the left.
- THE EVEN BOXES (2, 4 … 18, the smaller ones) hold the same arm FOLDED for driving: the hinge block at the left, the boom telescoped short, the crossbar folded narrower than the box's height with the two cradles swung in against it, all of it compact and filling its smaller box.
- Each pair, 1 and 2, 3 and 4, and so on, is one truck's arm, extended and folded, drawn alike. Pairs 1–2, 7–8 and 15–16 belong to old worn trucks: their arm's paint is faded and scuffed with a little rust; the rest are clean.
- Steel, paint and lamps only: no wheels, tyres or car on the cradles, no chains, no text, letters, numbers or logos.
